I2.3.5 Hull area factors

         (i) Associated with each hull area is an Area Factor that reflects the relative magnitude of
         the load expected in that area. The Area Factor (AF) for each hull area is listed in Table 4.

         (ii) In the event that a structural member spans across the boundary of a hull area, the
         largest hull area factor is to be used in the scantling determination of the member.

         (iii) Due to their increased manoeuvrability, ships having propulsion arrangements with
         azimuth thruster(s) or “podded” propellers are to have specially considered Stern Icebelt (Si)
         and Stern Lower (Sl) hull area factors.




                                                   I2-7                   IACS Req. 2006/Rev.4 2019

I2.13.1 Application

         I2.13.1.1 A ramming impact on the bow is the design scenario for the evaluation of the
         longitudinal strength of the hull.




                                                       I2-17                       IACS Req. 2006/Rev.4 2019
                                                                                                             I2


         I2.13.1.2 Intentional ramming is not considered as a design scenario for ships which are
I2       designed with vertical or bulbous bows, see I1.1.6. Hence the longitudinal strength
(cont)   requirements given in I2.13 is not to be considered for ships with stem angle stem equal to or
         larger than 80 deg.

         I2.13.1.3 Ice loads are only to be combined with still water loads. The combined stresses
         are to be compared against permissible bending and shear stresses at different locations
         along the ship’s length. In addition, sufficient local buckling strength is also to be verified.

APPROVE requires no current/prior issue or material question, all changes SUPPORTED and every supplied gap explicitly nonmaterial. REJECT needs an actionable code issue. Evidence uses supplied E IDs or {id,start?,end?,quote?}; paired start/end are character offsets in that evidence, not code. RDF_FACT citations use the whole fact. Optional quotes are checked exactly. location uses start/end and optional unit=lines (default) or characters, on the full current candidate; software extracts exact code. Context questions/dispositions have no location and need no invented defect. Assess each supplied C ID once. REGRESSION links an actionable zero-based issue index; UNRESOLVED blocks approval. For APPROVE assess each G ID with material=false and why; material gaps require questions. Software owns hashes, IDs and reconciliation. Review supplied prior issues without returning duplicate bookkeeping. Unsupported assertions, invented references/quotes and inconsistent decisions are invalid; citation interpretation remains model judgment.

I2.13.1 Application

         I2.13.1.1 A ramming impact on the bow is the design scenario for the evaluation of the
         longitudinal strength of the hull.




                                                       I2-17                       IACS Req. 2006/Rev.4 2019
                                                                                                             I2


         I2.13.1.2 Intentional ramming is not considered as a design scenario for ships which are
I2       designed with vertical or bulbous bows, see I1.1.6. Hence the longitudinal strength
(cont)   requirements given in I2.13 is not to be considered for ships with stem angle stem equal to or
         larger than 80 deg.

         I2.13.1.3 Ice loads are only to be combined with still water loads. The combined stresses
         are to be compared against permissible bending and shear stresses at different locations
         along the ship’s length. In addition, sufficient local buckling strength is also to be verified.

I2.3.5 Hull area factors

         (i) Associated with each hull area is an Area Factor that reflects the relative magnitude of
         the load expected in that area. The Area Factor (AF) for each hull area is listed in Table 4.

         (ii) In the event that a structural member spans across the boundary of a hull area, the
         largest hull area factor is to be used in the scantling determination of the member.

         (iii) Due to their increased manoeuvrability, ships having propulsion arrangements with
         azimuth thruster(s) or “podded” propellers are to have specially considered Stern Icebelt (Si)
         and Stern Lower (Sl) hull area factors.
